message.content: **What I did and why:** I researched Home Depot (HD) on the web and checked the live quote ($385.43 last, $385.41/$385.45 bid-ask), then bought 12 shares with a limit order at $386.00, which filled at $386.00 (≈$4,632 total — inside the $5,000 per-order cap and well under the $10,000 daily cap, and no funds moved out of the account). The available filing data (Home Depot's 10-K for the year ended 2024-01-28) shows a still very profitable but decelerating business: total net sales of $152,669M, operating income of $21,689M, net income of $15,143M, diluted EPS of $15.11 and operating cash flow of $21,172M — all down versus the prior year ($157,403M sales, $24,039M operating income, $17,105M net income, $16.69 diluted EPS), reflecting the soft housing/big-ticket demand backdrop, while the SRS Distribution acquisition adds sales growth and the franchise remains a cash-generative market leader at roughly 25x trailing earnings. Because the recent trend is mildly negative but the quality and cash generation are intact, I sized the position small and used a limit price essentially at the market rather than chasing; the only substantive news items I could retrieve beyond the filing were thin market roundups ("shares little changed as analysts weighed demand and the outlook"), so I kept the position modest. Note: the source page labels the 2023-01-29→2024-01-28 period "fiscal 2024," but I tagged the figures as fiscal year 2023, which is Home Depot's own designation for that year.
